newsitem.title: USA: Du Pont jury, in search of verdict, works late.
newsitem.headline: Du Pont jury, in search of verdict, works late.

text.p: Jurors in the John du Pont murder trial were ordered to work late on their fourth day of deliberations on Friday, after reviewing eyewitness testimony of the killing of Olympic champion wrestler David Schultz.
Court of Common Pleas Judge Patricia Jenkins ordered the jurors to work beyond their normal quitting time of 6:00 p.m., court spokesman John La Rosa told reporters.
The jurors appeared to be focusing on the moments before and immediately after the killing in a drawn-out struggle to determine what degree of homicide might be applicable under Pennsylvania law.

Since beginning deliberations on Tuesday afternoon, jurors have repeatedly returned to the courtroom to hear rereadings of testimony or jury instructions dealing with the three degrees of homicide with which du Pont has been charged -- first degree murder, third degree murder and voluntary manslaughter.
The six-man, six-woman jury had its longest uninterrupted stretch of deliberation on Friday afternoon after hearing rereadings of key testimony in the morning.
Jurors heard portions of testimony from Schultz's widow, Nancy, and Patrick Goodale, a du Pont security consultant who accompanied du Pont to Schultz's home on the day of the killing, Jan. 26, 1996.
Schultz was killed outside his home on the du Pont estate, where he was a coach at a training facility du Pont established.
Du Pont's lawyers have conceded du Pont killed Schultz, but are seeking a verdict of not guilty by reason of insanity, saying he was unaware of the wrongfulness of his acts.
In addition to verdicts of not guilty or not guilty by reason of insanity, the jurors can render verdicts of guilty or guilty but mentally ill.
